title: Growth by kind of work
question: Is growth a different thing in construction, professional services, software and grants to nonprofits?
finding: Grants to nonprofits account for the most added money: $3.99 billion across 280 measured agreements, 60% of which grew by a quarter or more (typical rise among those that grew: 92%). Goods and general services: 21 of 52 grew by a quarter or more (40%), $3.02 billion added; of those that grew, 8 read as more years at the same yearly cost, 8 as more years at a higher yearly cost and 11 as a higher ceiling for the same term. Other services: 33 of 114 grew by a quarter or more (29%), $1.40 billion added; of those that grew, 25 read as more years at the same yearly cost, 7 as more years at a higher yearly cost and 12 as a higher ceiling for the same term. Software and technology: 41 of 87 grew by a quarter or more (47%), $935.5 million added; of those that grew, 21 read as more years at the same yearly cost, 10 as more years at a higher yearly cost and 14 as a higher ceiling for the same term. Professional services: 41 of 83 grew by a quarter or more (49%), $599.7 million added; of those that grew, 16 read as more years at the same yearly cost, 5 as more years at a higher yearly cost and 21 as a higher ceiling for the same term. Construction: 0 of 6 grew by a quarter or more (0%), $8.6 million added; of those that grew, 0 read as more years at the same yearly cost, 0 as more years at a higher yearly cost and 1 as a higher ceiling for the same term. Only 6 construction agreements are in the Board's files at all: construction is awarded and changed under authority delegated to departments and their commissions, which is what the Budget and Legislative Analyst's two audits examine. The bid-sheet and official-review screens are the evidence for construction.
how: Board of Supervisors titles from 2014 to 2026 were linked into one record per agreement, following only links proven by a dollar figure carried from one title to the next or by a shared contract number (the rule used in the amendment-growth screen). The first amount is the total in the first approval on file or, where the first file is an amendment, the amount that amendment says it started from; the latest is the highest total approved. Left out: 527 leases and property; 225 no usable name in the title; 167 agreements with other public bodies; 164 no amount in any title; 58 loans; 21 agreements that bring money in (concessions, rents, franchises). The kind of work is read from the wording of the titles and from whether the other party is a nonprofit in the payment records: construction (build, design-build, sewer, paving); professional services (engineering, design, programme and construction management, consulting); software and technology; grants and service agreements with nonprofits; goods (vehicles, fuel, drugs, supplies); and other services. Each row is then read from its dates: if the end date did not move, it is "same term, higher ceiling"; if it moved and the ceiling per year of term stayed within 25% of the first, "more years at about the same yearly cost"; if the yearly figure rose by more, "more years and a higher yearly cost". Dates are taken from the wording of the titles (the latest date in a title is taken as the end it now runs to; "extend by two years" gives the end before).
limits: Each step here was approved in a public vote. Most of these are services the City chose to keep buying: a shelter, a treatment programme, a software licence or a security contract extended for more years at much the same yearly cost is a renewal, not an overrun, and the row says so where the dates allow. A ceiling is the most that may be spent, not what was spent; an as-needed or master agreement has a ceiling that is a limit on orders. Only agreements that needed a Board vote appear (under Charter section 9.118, broadly a contract of $10 million or more and a later amendment of more than $500,000 to one), so smaller contracts are absent, and so is nearly all construction, which departments and their commissions award and change under their own authority. Titles are text-mined: an amount or date can be misread, and each row links to its file. Pandemic emergency work explains several of the steepest rises in 2020 and 2021. Sorting by wording puts some agreements in the wrong kind. "Followed from the first approval" needs at least five agreements to show a share. Amounts, parties and dates taken from Board file titles are read by machine: in a hand check of 50 titles, 11 had at least one field read wrongly (4 after later fixes).
